utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see it. Let's see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness says "no" in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The date is December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you see that page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's number 01320783, and it says "List," and it has the date of December 1992. Do you see that, Mr. Rankic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB RANKIC
utterances.text: Nothing like that. I don't see 1992 in any of these documents. It is just not there. 1993, perhaps we can find something there. But in 1992, there was nothing. So this is the discrepancy I'm talking about in relation to documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So you're disagreeing with the date, you're not saying that you don't see a date.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB RANKIC
utterances.text: No, no date, no where to be found. This is a fabrication. No stamp, no date, nothing there. This was something that was tailored to their needs. I am not a legal expert myself, but as far as I can see, this --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, you've agreed with an earlier document, that you compiled it yourself, and that your signature is at the end of it. So surely you're not suggesting that even as far back as July 1992, no documents or records were being kept. You've put one of them together yourself.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB RANKIC
utterances.text: As I've said, I said which documents were produced in order to get something. That was what we were after, all of us. If that's what it takes, I'll be a company manager just to get some flesh flour. But this is not a proper document. There's not a stamp anywhere to be seen. These are documents that were handwritten by some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me intervene a little bit here, and then we'll stop for the day. You know with precision the date of the inception, of the creation, of the setting up, of the Bratunac Brigade, because you indicated it to us; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we were told is that the brigade had been set up. I wasn't there myself, but they said that it had been set up on the 14th of November, 1992, that's what we were told, at the Fontana Hotel. That's what we heard, but I knew nothing else about that. Whether it's true or not, I can't say. I never checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You also told us that, although you are mentioned as being the commander of the 4th Ceta of this Bratunac Brigade, in reality, you were nothing of the sort except that you were replacing Petar Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and that you were at the same time, all the time, in your village of Bjelovac at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you were at the time, in December 1992, in the village of Bjelovac and you never actually participated in the activities of the Bratunac Brigade, how do you know that the Bratunac Brigade, in December of 1992, did not have any mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The brigade did, but we back at Bjelovac had none. I didn't even lay eyes on Bratunac since 1992, only on the 27th, after the fall of Bjelovac, because we remained in Bjelovac throughout. That's why I'm saying this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you -- when this document says that the mortar section, or whatever it is, consisted of several persons, you are not in a position to confirm to us that, indeed, there was no mortar section in the Bratunac Brigade in December of 1992. You don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Guards, yes. Nothing wrong with that. I stood guard. But nothing aside from that, nothing else, in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I put it to you that there is nothing wrong with being a soldier or a commander in your own -- in your country's or in your government's army either. In times of need --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- if you are recruited, you are recruited, and you form part of the army. It's nothing to be ashamed of. No one is going to punish you because possibly you were a member of the Bratunac Brigade in 1992, or you were a commander of one of its platoons or cetas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, I became that. But in 1992, none of it, so there was a change there. That's why I'm saying I recognise nothing in relation to '92. In '93, I was a member of a mortar platoon, in '93. But back in '92, there was no such thing. That's where I see a discrepancy between what I've been presented with. But how come these documents are predated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are getting there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to a period before '93? That's what I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At which time in 1993 were you a member of a mortar platoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had a surgery in my thyroid gland, and I was not an able-bodied man to take part in military service, so they sent me to the signals unit of the mortar unit, because I'd had a surgery. That's where they sent me. I was part of that department, because that was the only post that I could fill. I was not able to do anything else because I had had a surgery. I was part of that squad. That's why I had the salary and that's why I received the rations, and that's what you can see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question was when in 1993 did you become a member of this signals or mortar platoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the exact date. I know that it did happen, but I can't give you the exact date. It's been 12 years, after all. I have zillions of other things to worry about. There's no document at hand to show that. But yes, it did happen back in 1993, that much is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think that it happened in the first half of 1993 or in the second half of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] '92 -- second half of '93/'94. Later I was with a platoon for a long time. I remained in the records of the platoon for a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jones, if you have any further questions for today, you can proceed. Otherwise, we can adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would simply put to the witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You've said, "I was a member of a mortar platoon." Before when I asked you that question you denied it. Why didn't you answer truthfully the first time I put the question to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB RANKIC
utterances.text: '93, in '92 -- I'm talking about '92. But '92, I came to answer questions about the year of 1992. No questions had been asked by that time about 1993. Where is a date? Can you show me a date? Because if it's about 1993, there must be a date. That's why I disagree, and that's what causes me to fail to answer any other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you could direct the witness that he's to answer questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D93 does not show a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The date -- I referred to the ERN number of the document, so I don't have the exhibit number in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last document that you tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Oh, indeed. Indeed. I never claimed that that document had a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put to the witness that he had been in a mortar platoon, without mentioning a date, and he denied that he had ever been a mortar platoon. And I would be grateful if Your Honour would direct the to answer questions regardless of dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think he has given you a sufficient answer. He said that when he answered that question, "I was referring to 1992," and not to any other specific date. And this document does not have a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honour. The question was whether he had ever served in a mortar platoon, but he's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he's telling you that he did in 1993, second half, towards 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not satisfied that that's a truthful answer. That's our position. And I'll move on to another subject tomorrow. I don't think there's any point pursuing it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think, witness, we will give you a rest now, and we will meet again tomorrow in the afternoon, at 2.15. Can you direct me which courtroom it is tomorrow? Courtroom II, this one. This is not conducive to -- anyway, this courtroom. Try to rest as much as you can, because tomorrow you've got a few -- how much longer do you expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Probably another hour, I would say, hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So try to get the next witness ready towards the end of the first session tomorrow, all right? Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of December, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
